content:
Isabella Rossi: seeing pretty nasty run-to-run variance on H100 in the harness. same commit + same container, tokens/s swings ~10–18% and TTFT p95 jumps around. anyone else seeing this?

Isabella Rossi: example (H100 SXM, llama-70b-ish prefill 2k, decode 256, bs=8, concurrency=16)
- run1: 18.9k tok/s, TTFT p95 410ms
- run2: 16.2k tok/s, TTFT p95 485ms
- run3: 19.1k tok/s, TTFT p95 418ms

Grace Kim: yep, I saw the same yesterday on the fp8 attention cases. at first thought it was kernel selection jitter but it correlates w/ node.

Rina Kobayashi: what cluster/region? and are you running on shared nodes or reserved bench pool?

Isabella Rossi: us-east bench pool (but not fully isolated). I grabbed 1x H100 from the general batch queue b/c bench pool was busy.

Grace Kim: that’s likely it. we’ve been getting contention. also clocks not pinned by default.

Irene Choi: +1 on contention. some of those nodes are still set up for mixed workloads. can you paste `nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK,POWER,TEMPERATURE` from a “slow” run?

Isabella Rossi: sure, from a slow run:
```
clocks.current.graphics : 1410 MHz
clocks.current.sm       : 1410 MHz
clocks.current.mem      : 2619 MHz
power.draw              : 585.34 W
power.limit             : 700.00 W
temperature.gpu         : 78 C
clocks.throttle_reasons
  sw_thermal_slowdown    : Active
  hw_thermal_slowdown    : Not Active
  hw_power_brake_slowdown: Not Active
```

Isabella Rossi: fast run on another node:
```
clocks.current.sm       : 1755 MHz
temperature.gpu         : 67 C
sw_thermal_slowdown     : Not Active
```

Vanessa Ortiz: those temps look like a hot box / bad airflow / neighbor job. some racks in us-east-3 have higher ambient; we’ve been tracking.

Rina Kobayashi: harness right now doesn’t do any clock pinning, right? it just logs device props.

Isabella Rossi: correct. it logs compute capability + total mem, but not clocks/power state (yet).

Marcus Reed: also check CPU side. if other workloads on the node, you get host contention (dataloader, tokenization, scheduler thread). are we pinning CPU affinity?

Isabella Rossi: not currently. just whatever k8s gives us.

Julian Moore: for scheduling benchmarks, even small CPU jitter can inflate TTFT if the queueing thread stalls. especially in mixed prefill/decode runs.

Grace Kim: propose we do 3 things:
1) run ONLY on reserved bench pool nodes (no shared)
2) pin GPU clocks + enable persistence
3) add “measurement stability” gating (discard warmup, require variance < X)

Rina Kobayashi: agreed. for (2), we can add an optional step in the runner:
- `nvidia-smi -pm 1`
- `nvidia-smi -lgc <min,max>` (or `-ac` if we want mem too)
- set power cap? (maybe leave default power limit)

Irene Choi: careful: `-lgc` requires admin perms on some clusters. bench pool nodes can allow it via daemonset; general pool won’t.

Vanessa Ortiz: we can make “bench nodes” label enforce exclusive allocation + enable clock locking. I’ll sync w/ Irene.

Rafael Mendes: from SRE side: if we’re going to canary gates later, we *need* harness artifacts to include thermal + throttle reasons. otherwise we chase ghosts.

Isabella Rossi: +1. I can add logging to artifact metadata:
- current clocks
- throttle reasons
- temperature
- driver/CUDA
and dump `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=... --format=csv` at start/end.

Grace Kim: also note that H100 auto-boost can drift in the first minute. we might need longer warmup. right now warmup is only 20 iters.

Omar El-Sayed: on mixed workloads, the first few batches are different due to cache + batch formation. we should ignore initial N seconds, not just N iterations.

Marcus Reed: +1. iteration counts don’t map well across kernels (some take longer). time-based warmup (e.g., 60s) + then sample for 120s.

Rina Kobayashi: ok, harness fix proposal:
- warmup for `--warmup_s 60`
- measure for `--measure_s 180`
- record per-second throughput histogram + p50/p95 across seconds
- fail job if coefficient of variation > 5% (configurable)

Isabella Rossi: I can implement this in the harness + runner. might be a fast PR.

Irene Choi: also, check driver mismatch. we had nodes in us-east on 550.54 and others on 550.76 last week.

Isabella Rossi: ugh. I did notice different output:
- slow node: Driver 550.54.14
- fast node: Driver 550.76.02

Grace Kim: that explains some of it too. kernel perf can shift w/ driver.

Vanessa Ortiz: we’re standardizing images this week but it’s not 100% yet. for the sprint, we should pin to a specific nodepool / image tag.

Rafael Mendes: for reproducibility: runner should refuse to run if driver/CUDA isn’t in an allowlist (or at least warn loudly and tag results).

Julian Moore: can we also ensure no MIG? I’ve seen “H100 80GB” but actually 1g.10gb slices in some test clusters.

Isabella Rossi: these are full GPUs (no MIG) but I can add a check: `nvidia-smi -L` + query MIG mode.

Hiro Tanaka: pulling up because this will invalidate kernel comparisons if not fixed. let’s treat as a blocker for full matrix runs.

Hiro Tanaka: action items:
- Isabella: add env + thermal/clock metadata + time-based warmup/measure + MIG check (PR today)
- Vanessa/Irene: confirm reserved bench pool nodes w/ consistent driver + clock-lock permissions
- Rina: update benchmark runbook checklist with “must run on bench pool + pinned versions”

Grace Kim: also, we should re-run the “variance case” after fixes and post a before/after plot so we can sanity-check.

Isabella Rossi: sounds good. I’ll rerun the same case on (a) shared node and (b) bench pool w/ clocks locked and post CV.

Rina Kobayashi: what clock target are we thinking? just lock at max SM clock?

Irene Choi: recommended for H100 SXM in our racks is `-lgc 1410,1755` (lets it boost but bounded) OR `-lgc 1755,1755` if stable thermals. if you lock max and thermals are marginal you can *increase* throttling.

Marcus Reed: maybe default to bounded range + log throttle reasons. if we see thermal slowdown active, the run is invalid.

Rafael Mendes: +1: declare invalid if `sw_thermal_slowdown` is active during measurement window.

Isabella Rossi: ok. I’ll add a per-second poll (every 1s) during measure window for temp/clocks/throttle flags and attach as artifact. if any throttle active for >5% of samples, mark run “unstable”.

Grace Kim: perfect. also might explain the TTFT regressions thread from earlier—if TTFT samples include throttled windows.

Hiro Tanaka: thanks. pls keep this thread updated w/ PR link + rerun results. once stable we proceed to ENG-7428 full matrix.

Isabella Rossi: will do. starting PR now; will @ here when up.
